summary: Markets are positioning ahead of Jackson Hole next week, where new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will speak for the first time since taking office in May — and unlike his predecessors, Warsh no longer telegraphs intentions in advance, giving the event genuine information value.
tweet: Warsh no longer tips his hand before meetings — and a 39% September hike probability does not bind him. Gold surges, dollar slides, and stocks grind higher ahead of the most unscripted Jackson Hole in years.
